newsitem.title: USA: Barrett Business farm labor license revoked.
newsitem.headline: Barrett Business farm labor license revoked.

text.p: Human resource management company Barrett Business Services Inc said its farm and forest labor contractor license was revoked by Oregon state based on allegations related to requirements.
The state's action, made through a default judgment, was based on charges Barrett purportedly violated requirements imposed on farm and forest labor contractors, it said.
The license revocation included civil penalties of $488,000, it said.

Oregon had previously notified Barrett, outlining alleged problems related to written documentation showing employment terms and conditions and workers' rights and remedies had been properly communicated to employees, the company said.
Barrett said the state prevailed because the company's law firm failed to file a response to the notice within the mandated 20-day period.

Chief Executive Officer William Sherertz said: "We believe the state's allegations are without merit, and due to an error, we apparently will not have the opportunity to defend our company and our customers."
Sherertz said the state did not allege mistreatment or abuse of employees and fines were levied for the alleged lack of proper written documentation.
"It's simply a matter of whether or not we have the paperwork -- and we do," he said. "We will continue to vigorously seek an equitable resolution."
